rows.user_input: What happens if unforeseen exceptional circumstances make contract performance excessively burdensome for the debtor?
retrieved_contexts:
[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 147]
The contract makes the law of the parties. It can be
revoked or altered only by mutual consent of the parties
or for reasons provided for by law.
When, however, as a result of exceptional and
unpredictable events of a general character, the
performance of the contractual obligation, without
becoming impossible, becomes excessively onerous in
such way as to threaten the debtor with exorbitant loss,
the judge may according to the circumstances, and after
taking into consideration the interests of both parties,
reduce to reasonable limits, the obligation that has
become excessive. Any agreement to the contrary is
void.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 217]
The debtor may by agreement accept liability for
unforeseen events and for cases of force majeure. The
debtor may by agreement be discharged from all liability
for his failure to perform the contractual obligation, with
the exception of liability arising from his fraud or gross
negligence.
The debtor may, nevertheless, stipulate that he shall not
be liable for fraud or gross negligence committed by
persons whom he employs for the performance of his
obligation.
Any clause discharging a person from responsibility for
unlawful acts, is void.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 215]
When specific performance by the debtor is impossible,
he will be condemned to pay damages for
nonperformance of his obligation, unless he establishes
that the impossibility of performance arose from a cause
beyond his control. The same principle will apply, if the
debtor is late in the performance of his obligation.
rows.response: If unforeseen exceptional circumstances make contract performance excessively burdensome for the debtor, the judge may, according to the circumstances and after taking into consideration the interests of both parties, reduce to reasonable limits the obligation that has become excessive. This is provided for in Article 147.
rows.reference: The judge may, according to the circumstances and after weighing both parties' interests, reduce the excessive obligation to a reasonable limit. Any agreement to the contrary is void.

rows.user_input: ماذا يحدث إذا جعلت ظروف استثنائية غير متوقعة تنفيذ العقد مرهقاً للمدين؟
retrieved_contexts:
[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 147]
( ١ ( العقد شريعة المتعاقدين ، فلا يجوز نقضه ولا تعديله إلا باتفاق
الطرفين ، أو للأسباب التى يقررها القانون.
( ٢ ( ومع ذلك إذا طرأت حوادث استثنائية عامة لم يكن فى الوسع توقعها
وترتب على حدوثها أن تنفيذ الإلتزام التعاقدى ، وان لم يصبح مستحيلا ،
صار مرهقا للمدين بحيث يهدده بخسارة فادحة ، جاز للقاضى تبعا
للظروف وسد الموازنة بين مصلحة الطرفين أن يرد الإلتزام المرهق إلى
الحد المعقول. ويقع باطلا كل اتفاق على خلاف ذلك.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 217]
( ١ ( يجوز الاتفاق على أن يتحمل المدين تبعة الحادث المفاجئ والقوة
القاهرة.
( ٢ ( وكذلك يجوز الاتفاق على إعفاء المدين من أية مسئولية تترتب على
عدم تنفيذ إلتزامه التعاقدى الا ما ينشأ عن غشه أو عن خطئه الجسيم ، ومع
ذلك يجوز للمدين أن يشترط عدم مسئوليته عن الغش أو الخطأ الجسيم
الذى يقع من أشخاص يستخدمهم فى تنفيذ إلتزامه.
( ٣ ( ويقع باطلا كل شرط يقضى بالإعفاء من المسئولية المترتبة على
العمل غير المشروع.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 157]
( ١ ( فى العقود الملزمة للجانبين ، إذا لم يوف أحد المتعاقدين بإلتزامه جاز
للمتعاقد الآخر بعد اعذاره المدين أن يطالب بتنفيذ العقد أو بفسخه ، مع
التعويض فى الهالتين أن كان له مقتض.
( ٢ ( ويجوز للقاضى أن يمنح المدين اجلا إذا اقتضت الظروف ذلك ، كما
يجوز له أن يرفض الفسخ إذا كان ما لم يرف به المدين قليل الأهمية
بالنسبة إلى الإلتزام فى جملته.
rows.response: إذا جعلت ظروف استثنائية غير متوقعة تنفيذ العقد مرهقاً للمدين، جاز للقاضى تبعا للظروف وسد الموازنة بين مصلحة الطرفين أن يرد الإلتزام المرهق إلى الحد المعقول. ويقع باطلا كل اتفاق على خلاف ذلك. (المادة 147)
rows.reference: The judge may, according to the circumstances and after weighing both parties' interests, reduce the excessive obligation to a reasonable limit. Any agreement to the contrary is void.

rows.user_input: In the absence of an applicable legal provision, what does the judge decide according to?
retrieved_contexts:
[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 1]
Provisions of laws govern all matters to which these
provisions apply in letter or spirit.
In the absence of a provision of a law that is applicable,
the Judge will decide according to custom and in the
absence of custom in accordance with the principles of
Moslem Law.
In the absence of such principles, the Judge will apply the
principles of natural justice and the rules of equity.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 200]
The judge shall decide, in the absence of any provision of
the law, whether a natural obligation exists.
There cannot ever be a natural obligation that is contrary
to public policy.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 346]
In the absence of an agreement or of a provision of the
law to the contrary, payment must be made as soon as
the obligation has been definitely created as a liability of
the debtor.
The judge may in exceptional cases and in the absence of
a provision of the law to the contrary, grant to the
debtor, when his position so requires, one or more
reasonable delays for the performance of his obligation,
provided that no serious prejudice is thereby caused to
the creditor.
rows.response: In the absence of an applicable legal provision, the judge decides according to custom. If there is no custom, the judge decides in accordance with the principles of Moslem Law. If there are no such principles, the judge applies the principles of natural justice and the rules of equity. (Article 1)
rows.reference: The judge decides according to custom, and in the absence of custom, according to the principles of Islamic (Moslem) law, and in the absence of such principles, according to natural justice and equity.

rows.user_input: إذا لم يوجد نص تشريعي ينطبق على مسألة معينة، فبماذا يحكم القاضي؟
retrieved_contexts:
[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 1]
(١) تسرى النصوص التشريعية على جميع المسائل التي تتناولها هذه
النصوص في لفظها أو في فحواها.
)٢( فإذا لم يوجد نص تشريعي يمكن تطبيقه، حكم القاضي بمقتضى
العرف، فإذا لم يوجد، فبمقتضى مبادئ الشريعة الإسلامية، فإذا لم يوجد
فبمقتضى مبادئ القانون الطبيعي وقواعد العدالة.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 200]
يقدر القاضى ، عند عدم النص ، ما إذا كان هناك إلتزام طبيعى. وفى كل
حال لا يجوز أن يقوم إلتزام طبيعى يخالف النظام العام.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 32]
يسرى في شأن المفقود والغائب الأحكام المقررة في قوانين خاصة ، فان لم
توجد فأحكام الشريعة الإسلامية.
rows.response: إذا لم يوجد نص تشريعي ينطبق على مسألة معينة، فيحكم القاضي بمقتضى العرف. وإذا لم يوجد العرف، فيحكم القاضي بمقتضى مبادئ الشريعة الإسلامية. وإذا لم يوجد مبادئ الشريعة الإسلامية، فيحكم القاضي بمقتضى مبادئ القانون الطبيعي وقواعد العدالة. هذا ما ورد في المادة ١ من القانون المدني المصري.
rows.reference: The judge decides according to custom, and in the absence of custom, according to the principles of Islamic (Moslem) law, and in the absence of such principles, according to natural justice and equity.

rows.user_input: How can a legal provision be repealed?
retrieved_contexts:
[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 2]
A provision of a law can only be repealed by a
subsequent law expressly providing for such repeal, or
containing a provision inconsistent with a provision of
the former law or regulating anew a matter previously
regulated by a former law.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 845]
Partition by agreement may be rescinded if one of the
co-partitioners succeeds in proving that he has been
injured to the extent of more than one fifth of his share,
on the basis of the value of the property at the time of
the partition.
The action for rescission must be commenced within the
year following the partition. The defendant can stop the
action and prevent the new partition, by giving the
plaintiff the amount by which his share is short in money
or in kind.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 149]
When a contract of adhesion contains leonine
conditions, the judge may modify these conditions or
relieve the adhering party of the obligation to perform
these conditions in accordance with the principles of
equity. Any agreement to the contrary is void.
rows.response: A legal provision can only be repealed by a subsequent law that expressly provides for such repeal, or by a subsequent law containing a provision inconsistent with a provision of the former law or regulating anew a matter previously regulated by a former law. This is stipulated in Article 2 of the Egyptian Civil Code.
rows.reference: A provision of law can only be repealed by a subsequent law that expressly provides for repeal, contains a provision inconsistent with the earlier law, or regulates anew a matter already regulated by the earlier law.

rows.user_input: At what age does a person reach legal majority in Egypt?
retrieved_contexts:
[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 33]
Egyptian nationality is governed by a special law.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 44]
All persons attaining majority in possession of their
mental faculties and not under legal disability, have full
legal capacity to exercise their civil rights.
The majority of a person is fixed at twenty one years
completed in accordance with the Gregorian calendar.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 11]
The status and the legal capacity of persons are
governed by the law of the country to which they belong
by reason of their nationality. If, however, in a
transaction of a pecuniary nature, concluded and having
effect in Egypt, one of the parties is a foreigner without
legal capacity and such lack of capacity is due to a
reason that is not apparent and which cannot be easily
detected by the other party, this reason has no effect on
his legal capacity.
The legal status of foreign juristic persons such as
companies, associations, foundations, or others, is
subject to the law of the State in whose territory such
juristic persons have established their actual principal
seat of management. If, however, a juristic person
carries on its principal activities in Egypt, Egyptian law
will be applied.
rows.response: In Egypt, a person reaches legal majority at the age of twenty one years completed, as stipulated in Article 44.
rows.reference: A person attaining majority in possession of their mental faculties, and not under legal disability, has full legal capacity. Majority is fixed at twenty-one complete Gregorian years.

rows.user_input: في أي سن يبلغ الشخص سن الرشد القانوني في مصر؟

(٢) وسن الرشد هى إحدى وعشرون سنة ميلادية كاملة.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 46]
كل من بلغ سن التمييز ولم يبلغ سن الرشد وكل من بلغ سن الرشد وكان
سفيهاً أو ذا غفلة ' يكون ناقص الأهلية وفقاً لما يقرره القانون.

(١) لا يكون أهلا لمباشرة حقوقه المدنية من كان فاقد التمييز لصغر في

rows.response: في مصر، يبلغ الشخص سن الرشد القانوني في سن إحدى وعشرين سنة ميلادية كاملة، وفقاً لنص المادة 44 من Egyptian Civil Code.
rows.reference: A person attaining majority in possession of their mental faculties, and not under legal disability, has full legal capacity. Majority is fixed at twenty-one complete Gregorian years.

rows.user_input: What is the basic legal definition of a contract of sale?
retrieved_contexts:
[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 418]
Sale is a contract whereby the vendor binds himself to
transfer to the purchaser the ownership of a thing or any
other propriety right in consideration of a price in
money.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 467]
If the owner ratifies the sale, the contract will become
binding on him and valid as regards the purchaser.
The sale will also become valid as regards the purchaser
if the ownership of the thing sold devolves upon the
vendor subsequently to the conclusion of the contract.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 89]
A contract is created, subject to any special formalities
that may be required by law for its conclusion, from the
moment that two persons have exchanged two
concordant intentions.
rows.response: The basic legal definition of a contract of sale is a contract whereby the vendor binds himself to transfer to the purchaser the ownership of a thing or any other propriety right in consideration of a price in money. This is outlined in [Article 418].
rows.reference: Sale is a contract whereby the vendor binds himself to transfer to the purchaser the ownership of a thing, or another proprietary right, in consideration of a price in money.

rows.user_input: ما هو التعريف القانوني الأساسي لعقد البيع؟
retrieved_contexts:
[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 418]
البيع عقد يلتزم بع البائع أن ينقل للمشتري ملكية شيء أو حقا ماليا أخر في
مقابل ثمن نقدي.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 430]
(١) إذا كان البيع مؤجل الثمن ، جاز للبائع أن يشترط أن يكون نقل الملكية
إلى المشتري موقوفا على استيفاء الثمن كله ولو تم تسليم المبيع.
) (٢ فإذا كان الثمن يدفع أقساطا ، جاز للمتعاقدين أن يتفقا على أن يستبقي
البائع جزءا منه تعويضا له عن فسخ البيع إذا لم توف جميع الأقساط . ومع
ذلك يجوز للقاضي تبعا للظروف أن يخفض التعويض المتفق عليه وفقا
للفقرة الثانية من المادة .٢٢٤
) (٣ وإذا وفيت الأقساط جميعا ، فان انتقال الملكية إلى المشتري يعتبر
مستندا إلى وقت البيع .
(٤) وتسري أحكام الفقرات الثلاث السابقة ولو سمي المتعاقدان البيع
إيجارا.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 419]
(١( يجب أن يكون المشتري عالما بالبيع علما كافيا ، ويعتبر العلم كافيا إذا
اشتمل العقد على بيان المبيع وأوصافه الأساسية بيانا يمكن من تعرفه.
(٢( وإذا ذكر في عقد البيع أن المشتري عالم بالمبيع ، سقط حقه في طلب
إبطال البيع بدعوى عدم علمه به إلا إذا أثبت تدليس البائع.
rows.response: عقد البيع هو عقد يلتزم فيه البائع أن ينقل للمشتري ملكية شيء أو حقا ماليا آخر في مقابل ثمن نقدي، وفقا للفقرة الأولى من المادة 418.
rows.reference: Sale is a contract whereby the vendor binds himself to transfer to the purchaser the ownership of a thing, or another proprietary right, in consideration of a price in money.

rows.user_input: How long after delivery can a purchaser claim on a warranty for defects in a thing sold?
retrieved_contexts:
[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 455]
When a vendor has warranted the proper working of the
thing sold for an agreed period of time, the purchaser, in
the case of a defect subsequently appearing in the thing
sold, must, under pain of forfeiture of his right to the
warranty and subject to any agreement to the contrary,
give notice to the vendor within one month from the
date of the appearance of the defect and commence an
action within six months from the date of notification.
Obligation of the Purchaser

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 452]
An action on a warranty is prescribed in one year from
the time of delivery of the thing sold, even if the
purchaser discovers the defect after the expiration of
this delay, unless the vendor agrees to be bound by the
warranty for a longer period.
The vendor, however, cannot avail himself of the
prescription of one year if it is proved that he has
fraudulently concealed the defect from the purchaser.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 434]
In a case of deficiency or excess in the thing sold, the
right of the purchaser to apply for a reduction of the
price or for cancellation of the contract, and the right of
the vendor to claim that the price be made up, are both
prescribed within one year from the date of the actual
delivery of the thing sold.
rows.response: The purchaser can claim on a warranty for defects in a thing sold within one year from the time of delivery of the thing sold, as provided in Article 452. If the purchaser discovers the defect after the expiration of this delay, the action on the warranty is still prescribed within one year from the time of delivery, unless the vendor agrees to be bound by the warranty for a longer period. Additionally, the purchaser must give notice to the vendor within one month from the date of the appearance of the defect and commence an action within six months from the date of notification, as stipulated in Article 455.
rows.reference: An action on a warranty is prescribed one year from the time of delivery, even if the defect is discovered after that period, unless the vendor agreed to a longer warranty period or fraudulently concealed the defect.

rows.user_input: كم من الوقت بعد التسليم يمكن للمشتري المطالبة بالضمان عن عيوب المبيع؟
retrieved_contexts:
[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 455]
إذا ضمن البائع صلاحية المبيع للعمل مدة معلومة ثم ظهر خلل في المبيع ،
فعلي المشتري أن يخطر البائع بهذا الخلل في مدة شهر من ظهوره وأن
يرفع الدعوى في مدة ستة شهور من هذا الإخطار ، وإلا سقط حقه في
الضمان ، كل هذا ما لم يتفق على غيره.
التزامات المشتري

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 447]
(١( يكون البائع ملزما بالضمان إذا لم يتوافر في المبيع وقت التسليم
الصفات التي كفل للمشتري وجودها فيه ، أو إذا كان بالمبيع عيب ينقص
من قيمته أو من نفعه بحسب الغاية المقصودة مستفادة مما هو مبين في
العقد أو مما هو ظاهر من طبيعة الشيء ، أو الغرض الذي أعد له ،
ويضمن البائع هذا العيب ولو لم يكن عالما بوجوده.
(٢( ومع ذلك لا يضمن البائع العيوب التي كان المشتري يعرفها وقت البيع
، أو كان يستطيع أن يتبينها بنفسه لو أنه فحص المبيع بعناية الرجل العادي
، إلا إذا أثبت المشتري أن البائع قد أكد له خلو المبيع من هذا العيب ، أو
أثبت أن البائع قد تعمد إخفاء العيب غشا منه.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 450]
إذا أخطر المشتري البائع بالعيب في الوقت الملائم كان له أن يرجع
بالضمان على النحو المبين في المادة .٤٤٤
rows.response: يمكن للمشتري المطالبة بالضمان عن عيوب المبيع خلال ستة شهور من إخطار البائع بالعيب، وذلك وفقًا لأحكام المادة 455 من Egyptian Civil Code.
rows.reference: An action on a warranty is prescribed one year from the time of delivery, even if the defect is discovered after that period, unless the vendor agreed to a longer warranty period or fraudulently concealed the defect.

rows.user_input: Where must a purchaser pay the price, absent a contrary agreement?
retrieved_contexts:
[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 656]
In the absence of a custom or an agreement to the
contrary the price is payable upon delivery of the works.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 456]
Subject to a clause or custom to the contrary, the price is
payable at the place where the delivery of the thing sold
is made.
If the price is not payable at the time of delivery of the
thing sold, payment must be made at the domicile of the
purchaser on due date.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 348]
In the absence of an agreement or a provision of the law
to the contrary, expenses in connection with payment
are at the charge of the debtor.
rows.response: In the absence of a contrary agreement, the purchaser must pay the price at the place where the delivery of the thing sold is made, as provided in Article 456. If the price is not payable at the time of delivery, payment must be made at the domicile of the purchaser on due date, as also provided in Article 456.
rows.reference: Subject to a clause or custom to the contrary, the price is payable at the place where delivery of the thing sold is made.

rows.user_input: أين يجب على المشتري دفع الثمن في حال عدم وجود اتفاق مخالف؟
retrieved_contexts:
